instruction: Rewrite this networking note into the vault house style. Keep operational concerns concise, preserve protocol relationship sections, and normalize Obsidian links.
input_markdown:
# TLS
## Basics
TLS, Transport Layer Security, provides encryption, integrity and peer authentication for network communication.
## What TLS Adds
- confidentiality through encryption
- integrity checks for transmitted data
- certificate based server authentication
## Common Use Cases
- HTTPS for secure web traffic over [HTTP](/HTTP.md)
- encrypted API communication
- secure database and service to service connections
## Relationship to Other Protocols
TLS usually runs on top of reliable transport such as [TCP](/TCP and UDP.md) and is commonly layered under protocols like [HTTP](/HTTP.md).
## Common Operational Concerns
- certificate expiration
- hostname mismatch
- unsupported protocol or cipher versions
## Related Notes
- [HTTP](/HTTP.md)
- [TCP and UDP](/TCP and UDP.md)
